task.title: Font resources and descriptors
task.shortdesc: Use @font-face to make a font face available to a stylesheet. The rule names the family, identifies one or more sources and describes the face so the font matcher can choose it.

context.p: The descriptors inside the rule describe the font face, not the selected XML element. Use separate rules for separate faces in the family, such as regular, bold and italic faces. A rule needs valid font-family and src descriptors. Invalid declarations are ignored. When a descriptor occurs more than once, the last valid value is used.

info.p: CSS Fonts 4 §4.2, Font family descriptor.

This descriptor gives the face the family name used by a font-family property. It replaces family names stored in the font file. Write the name as a quoted string or as one or more unquoted identifiers. Separate words in an unquoted name with spaces. A name that is a CSS-wide keyword must be quoted. A declared family name also takes precedence over an installed family with the same name.
CSS Fonts 4 §4.3, Font reference descriptor; parsing; source selection; CSS Fonts 5 src descriptor.

This descriptor is a comma-separated, ordered list of sources. Each source is either a URL with optional hints or a local() reference. When choosing a source, a processor checks the entries in order and can skip entries whose declared format or technology it does not support.

url() identifies a font resource. A relative URL is resolved against the stylesheet’s base URL. local() identifies an installed font by its full name or PostScript name. It does not refer to a file. The processor tries sources in order and proceeds to the next source if it cannot find or use the current one.
CSS Fonts 4 format() hint; font format definitions.
The optional format() hint identifies a URL resource’s format. Use one format keyword or a quoted format string.

ul.li: collection identifies a TrueType or OpenType font collection, which can contain multiple font faces.
embedded-opentype identifies Embedded OpenType resources.
opentype identifies OpenType resources. It does not promise a particular glyph outline format or that the font contains OpenType layout tables.
svg identifies an SVG font.
truetype identifies TrueType resources.
woff identifies WOFF 1.0 resources.
woff2 identifies WOFF 2.0 resources.

info.p: The opentype and truetype hints are treated as synonyms by CSS Fonts. The hint lets a processor avoid a resource format it cannot use. It does not convert the resource.

For compatibility with older stylesheets, CSS Fonts 4 also accepts these quoted forms: format("woff2") , format("woff") , format("truetype") , format("opentype") and format("collection") . They mean the corresponding unquoted format keywords.
The legacy strings "woff2-variations" , "woff-variations" , "truetype-variations" and "opentype-variations" mean the corresponding format keyword followed by tech(variations).
CSS Fonts 4 tech() hint; font technology definitions.
The optional tech() function lists technologies required by the resource. Separate multiple values with commas. The processor can skip the source if it does not support any listed requirement.

ul.li: features-opentype , features-aat and features-graphite indicate support for OpenType, Apple Advanced Typography or Graphite layout features, respectively.
color-COLRv0 and color-COLRv1 indicate color glyphs in the corresponding COLR table versions.
color-SVG indicates SVG color glyphs.
color-sbix indicates the sbix bitmap color glyph format.
color-CBDT indicates the CBDT bitmap color glyph format.
variations indicates support for font variation axes.
palettes indicates color-font palette support.
incremental indicates support for incremental font transfer.
avar2 indicates support for OpenType version 2 axis variations, which remap variable-font axes.

info.p: format() precedes tech() when a source uses both. The four -variations strings listed above each mean the corresponding format hint plus tech(variations).

step.cmd: Describe which face the source provides

info.p: CSS Fonts 4 font property descriptors; weight values.

This descriptor tells the font matcher which weight or weight range the face provides. auto uses the weight information in the font. Otherwise, provide one absolute weight or two ascending endpoints. Two endpoints include every weight in the interval.

ul.li: normal is 400.
bold is 700.
A number from 1 through 1000 gives the weight directly. Larger numbers mean heavier weights.

info.p: The descriptor’s range tells the matcher which requested weights this face can satisfy. It does not change the font’s data.
CSS Fonts 4 font property descriptors; width values.

This descriptor tells the matcher which width or width range the face provides. auto uses the width information in the font. Otherwise, provide one value or two ascending endpoints. A non-negative percentage represents glyph width relative to normal width. Values below 100% are narrower; values above 100% are wider.
The named values correspond to these percentages:

ul.li: ultra-condensed : 50%.
extra-condensed : 62.5%.
condensed : 75%.
semi-condensed : 87.5%.
normal : 100%.
semi-expanded : 112.5%.
expanded : 125%.
extra-expanded : 150%.
ultra-expanded : 200%.

info.p: The legacy descriptor name font-stretch is an alias for font-width.
CSS Fonts 4 font property descriptors; style values.
This descriptor tells the matcher which style or style range the face provides. auto uses the style information in the font.

ul.li: normal describes an upright face with no slant.
italic describes an italic face. If one is unavailable, matching can use an oblique face.
left describes an italic or oblique face with a positive, clockwise slant.
right describes an italic or oblique face with a negative, counter-clockwise slant.

oblique describes a slanted face. It can take one angle or two ascending endpoints from -90deg to 90deg. With no angle, the value is 14deg. Positive angles are clockwise; negative angles are counter-clockwise.

info.p: Two values define an inclusive angle range. Fractional angles are allowed.
CSS Fonts 5 font size descriptor.

This descriptor limits the font sizes for which the face is a match. auto matches any size. One number matches that size; two numbers define an inclusive range. The values are unitless numbers, not CSS lengths.
CSS Fonts 4 font-named-instance descriptor.

This descriptor selects a named instance in a variable font. auto leaves instance selection to the normal font variation process. A string selects the first named instance whose localized name matches the string. If no such instance exists, the descriptor behaves as auto. The requested font-weight, font-width, and font-style variation values are applied before the named instance’s axis values.
CSS Fonts 4 character range descriptor.
This descriptor gives the Unicode code points for which the face is eligible. Its value is a comma-separated list:

ul.li: A single code point has a form such as U+0041.
A range has a form such as U+0400-04FF. Both endpoints are included.
A wildcard uses one or more trailing question marks, as in U+4??. Each question mark stands for one hexadecimal digit.

info.p: Hexadecimal digits are ASCII case-insensitive. Endpoints must be valid Unicode code points, and a range’s end cannot precede its start. The descriptor filters the characters for which the face can be considered. It does not guarantee that the font contains a glyph for each one. The default range includes all Unicode code points.
CSS Fonts 4 font display descriptor.

This descriptor controls the font’s loading behavior while text is being displayed. The processor divides loading into a block period, when text may be invisible, and a swap period, when a loaded font may replace the fallback.

ul.li: auto lets the processor choose the policy.
block uses an invisible-text block period, then allows the downloaded font to replace the fallback.
swap shows fallback text immediately and allows the downloaded font to replace it.
fallback allows a short block period and a limited swap period. A late font load does not replace the fallback.
optional allows a very short block period and no swap period. The processor may use the font only when it is available promptly.

info.p: The user agent determines the durations of the block and swap periods.
CSS Fonts 4 font language override descriptor.

This descriptor sets the OpenType language-system tag used for the face’s language-sensitive features. normal uses the language selected for the text. A string supplies a case-sensitive OpenType language-system tag, such as "SRB". Find tags in the font’s documentation or in Microsoft’s OpenType language system tags. These are not BCP 47 tags such as sr or sr-Latn; use BCP 47 tags in xml:lang to identify the text’s language. The OpenType tag is matched as four characters; shorter strings are padded at the end with U+0020 spaces. Unknown tags are ignored.
CSS Fonts 4 font feature settings descriptor; feature tag values.

This descriptor sets initial low-level OpenType feature settings for the face. It does not affect font selection. normal makes no explicit change to glyph selection or positioning. Otherwise, give a comma-separated list of feature tags. Each tag is a case-sensitive string of exactly four printable ASCII characters. A tag can be followed by an integer, on or off . If the value is omitted, it is 1. on means 1; off means 0. 0 disables the feature. For a boolean feature, 1 enables it. For a non-boolean feature, an integer of 1 or greater enables it and selects that feature index. Tags that the font does not contain are ignored. See the feature tag value syntax.
CSS Fonts 4 font variation settings descriptor.

This descriptor sets initial low-level variation-axis settings for the face. It does not affect font selection. normal does not request additional axis settings. Otherwise, give a comma-separated list of case-sensitive axis tags paired with numbers, such as "wght" 650. An axis tag is a string of exactly four printable ASCII characters. Each number is an axis value; values outside the range supported by the font are clamped to that range. An axis tag the font does not contain is ignored. See the font-variation-settings property for the axis-tag rules. Prefer font-weight, font-width or font-style for the standard weight, width and slant axes. Those properties express the requested font characteristics and can also match non-variable faces.
CSS Fonts 5 glyph size multiplier descriptor.

This descriptor scales a face’s glyph outlines and associated metrics by a non-negative percentage. 100% leaves them unchanged. Other values scale glyphs, advances and metrics together. The CSS font-size remains unchanged.
CSS Fonts 5 font metrics override descriptors.

ascent-override replaces the ascent metric. descent-override replaces the descent metric. line-gap-override replaces the line-gap metric. Each accepts normal or a non-negative percentage. The percentage replaces the corresponding metric with that percentage of the effective font size after adjustment. normal uses the metric from the font as if the descriptor were absent. Each descriptor accepts one value for the x-axis and an optional second value for the y-axis. The second value defaults to normal.
CSS Fonts 5 superscript and subscript metric override descriptors.

superscript-position-override and subscript-position-override replace the corresponding glyph position metrics. superscript-size-override and subscript-size-override replace their glyph size metrics. These metrics are used when font-variant-position synthesizes superscript or subscript glyphs.
Each descriptor accepts normal, from-font or a percentage. For a position descriptor, the percentage can be positive or negative. For a size descriptor, it cannot be negative.

ul.li: normal lets the processor choose the metric from the font or a heuristic.
from-font uses the corresponding font metric when present. If it is absent, it behaves as normal.
A percentage replaces the metric with that percentage of the used font size.

info.p: The descriptors accept one value for the x-axis and an optional second value for the y-axis. If the second value is omitted, the x-axis value is used. The y-axis metric is used for upright text in vertical typographic modes.
